topic: Demobilization of the Cape Ann FSRU (2025-2026)
wiki_text: On 25 November 2025, TotalEnergies announced it would demobilize its floating LNG terminal in the Port of Le Havre, stating that with gas supply conditions in France and Europe having stabilized, the terminal was 'no longer necessary'; the company noted the facility had seen minimal utilization. The decision followed a 16 October 2025 ruling by the Rouen Administrative Court, which — after legal challenges by environmental organizations questioning the terminal's necessity and citing environmental risks — ordered the State to revoke within two months the decree that had authorized the terminal's installation. The chartered FSRU Cape Ann (built 2010, ~145,130 m3, owned/operated by Hoegh LNG, now Hoegh Evi), in service at Le Havre since 26 October 2023, departed the port by around 22 January 2026. The terminal had a nameplate regasification capacity of about 5 bcm/year, of which TotalEnergies had contracted roughly 50%, with the remainder marketed under regulator-approved rules.
